note: Baseline for the whole-tree security sweep (Issue #4193). Run `deno task security-tree-sweep` from worker/deno (or `deno run --allow-read --allow-write --allow-run --allow-env worker/deno/mod.ts security-tree-sweep --slug stSoftwareAU/VibeCoder` from the repository root). Every deduplicated finding the sweep reports must either be fixed or appear in exactly one list here. `falsePositives` entries need a `reason` explaining why the match is benign, `evidence` (one or more repository-relative `path:line` citations of the defence, type constraint or non-attacker origin that eliminates the finding, each resolving to a file and line in the tree) and a `line` or `snippet` anchor (an entry with neither would suppress every finding of the rule in the file) (Issue #3658). `accepted` entries are real but tolerated risks: they need a `reason` and should carry the tracking `issue` number, and need no `evidence`. Entries match on `path` plus `rule` (a rule family such as `command-injection`, or a tool-native rule id) and on a `line` anchor within the sweep's 10-line window (optional for `accepted`) or a `snippet` (the normalised source line), which is matched instead of `line` when present. The sweep exits non-zero while any finding is unlisted; a stale entry (matching nothing) is reported so it can be removed. A finding the worker scan alone reported is NOT baseline material: it mirrors an open `security` issue, so the sweep classifies it `tracked` and it clears when that issue closes (Issue #1518).

falsePositives.reason: `field` iterates the worker's own config-schema field names (identifier characters only), matched against the worker's own source tree — no untrusted input reaches the pattern (Issue #4193 triage of semgrep detect-non-literal-regexp).

Detection heuristics for LLM API hosts in scanned code (the `api.` host patterns): an unanchored host pattern over-matches (`api.anthropic.com.evil`), and over-matching is the safe direction for a detector that only flags for review (Issue #4409 CodeQL js/regex/missing-regexp-anchor).

Detection heuristic for the Google Generative Language API host, split into its own cluster when the pattern list grew past the sweep's 10-line window: an unanchored host pattern over-matches (`generativelanguage.googleapis.com.evil`), and over-matching is the safe direction for a detector that only flags for review (Issue #4409 CodeQL js/regex/missing-regexp-anchor).

The pattern requires `/` immediately after `github.com`, so a look-alike host (`github.com.evil/`) does not match; the extracted URLs are then validated against the repository slug downstream (Issue #4409 CodeQL js/regex/missing-regexp-anchor).
Test assertions that generated text contains issue URLs are not sanitisation (Issue #4409 CodeQL triage).

The flagged comparison IS the null guard the `typeof x === "object"` idiom requires: `typeof null` is `"object"`, so dropping `value !== null` is the bug the rule reads it as. CodeQL narrows `value` to `object` from the first conjunct and then objects to comparing that narrowed type with null — an artefact of its own inference, not a defect (Issue #1518 triage, js/comparison-between-incompatible-types).

falsePositives.snippet: if (typeof raw !== "object" || raw === null) return undefined;
falsePositives.reason: Same idiom and same analyser artefact as `container_extension_config.ts`: `typeof null` is `"object"`, so the `raw === null` arm is the guard that makes the narrowing sound. Removing it to satisfy the rule would reintroduce the null dereference it is there to stop (Issue #1518 triage, js/comparison-between-incompatible-types).

Deliberate, and the missing space is the point: the fixture is assembled from halves so this test file does not itself contain the literal `assertLinearGrowth`, which the manifest scan under test searches for. Written whole, the fixture would classify its own test file as measuring wall-clock time. Same triage as the `export_branding_test.ts` split fixtures (Issue #1518 triage, js/missing-space-in-concatenation).

accepted.reason: The `minimumReleaseAge: "0"` the rule flags is the documented first-party exemption for stSoftwareAU/* packages only (Issue #2124); every third-party ecosystem keeps the 24 hours set at the top of the file. Not the emergency override path (docs/security-advisory-triage.md).

`held` is provably true here — the acquire loop only `break`s after setting it and every other exit throws — so the rule is correct. Kept deliberately: the release path states the invariant it depends on, and a future exit added to that loop would make the guard load-bearing. A code-quality observation, not a security finding (js/trivial-conditional).

`timedOut`/`runFinished` are closure flags set from timer and completion callbacks, so the re-check before arming the next watchdog is not redundant at runtime even where the analyser proves it constant along one path. The same guard appears on the arming and wind-down paths and this one entry covers every occurrence — a second entry with the identical snippet could never match, because the fingerprint lookup stops at the first. A code-quality observation, not a security finding (js/trivial-conditional).

The write is the last one on the flag, so the analyser is right that nothing reads it. Kept deliberately: it is the second half of the `if (!fleetSummaryEmitted)` guard that stops the fleet summary being emitted twice (Issue #855), and the `finally` block it sits in is exactly where a later `await` would be appended — dropping the write would make the guard silently wrong then. A code-quality observation, not a security finding (Issue #1518 triage, js/useless-assignment-to-local).
